title: Doubt and Denial in the Past

sections.content:
When you doubt or deny an event that supposedly already occurred in the past, use the present perfect subjunctive:

• *Dudo que hayan terminado todo el trabajo.* (I doubt they finished all the work.)
• *No creo que Juan haya dicho semejante cosa.* (I don't think Juan said such a thing.)
• *No es verdad que hayamos perdido los billetes.* (It's not true that we lost the tickets.)
• *¿Crees que haya salido ya el tren?* (Do you think the train has left already?)

sections.title: Rules and Patterns
rows: No creo que haya dicho eso.
No es cierto que hayamos perdido.
Es dudoso que haya ocurrido así.

items.spanish: No creo que hayan entendido la explicación.
items.english: I don't think they understood the explanation.

items.spanish: Dudo que el tren haya llegado con puntualidad.
items.english: I doubt the train arrived on time.

items.spanish: No es verdad que nos hayamos olvidado de tu cumpleaños.
items.english: It's not true that we forgot your birthday.

sections.content: Affirmative *creo que* takes indicative (*Creo que ha venido*), but negative *no creo que* triggers subjunctive (*No creo que haya venido*).
